title: DecisionRecorded payload and the ingest rule into the central ledger are not defined in the source documents
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slide 42) and 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 14 and 16)
section: 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.4 Events consumed; 12.5 Workflows and activities
description: Architecture v5 slide 42 names only the producer (all 19), the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 and the consumers (rwb-decision and rwb-reporting) for DecisionRecorded. The Temporal and Drools design names the fields of the local decision record (chain_seq, inputsRef, ruleId, ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, actions, outcome, decidedAt, prev_hash, entry_hash) but not the event payload. No source states the dedupe key, the ordering rule, the rule by which rwb-decision assigns chain_seq and prev_hash when it ingests an event into the central ledger, or the catch-up window; the five-minute figure appears only in a slide note. The harness of this integration story and the ingest activity cannot be written against a payload and a rule that no source fixes.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 DecisionRecorded (producer all 19, topic rwb.decision-record.v1, consumers rwb-decision and rwb-reporting) and slide 11 (inbox dedupe, key caseId); Temporal and Drools design slide 11 (state change, decision record and outbox row in one transaction), slide 14 note (record collected into the central ledger within 5 minutes) and slide 16 note (record fields, JOB-14 checks the chain at 02:00); no AsyncAPI document for the shared topic is in the source set.
proposed: Publish the AsyncAPI document for rwb.decision-record.v1 with the DecisionRecorded payload and the ingest rule (CloudEvents id as the dedupe key in processed_event, order per case from the producer, chain_seq and prev_hash assigned by rwb-decision under the chain lock, catch-up within five minutes) at the shared-topic contract review before the first SIT run.

title: The owning rwb_* schema of the 24 operational dictionary objects is not stated
source: Ownership Map v1; RWB-E1-001 section 13 (the 24 operational objects of OPS 13, AGT 8 and RPT 3); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41
description: The dictionary holds 122 sys_objects rows: 98 name a data product and 24 carry none, the 13 OPS objects, the 8 AGT objects and the 3 RPT objects. The Ownership Map names business tables, including the agent, reporting and integration tables, but no source states object by object which rwb_* schema and login hold those 24 operational objects, so the estate cannot be fully resolved from the sources.
evidence: RWB-E1-001 section 13: sys_objects.data_product is nullable, so the 98 product objects name DP01 to DP14 and the 24 operational objects of OPS (13), AGT (8) and RPT (3) leave it empty. Ownership Map v1 names business, agent, reporting and integration tables; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 gives one schema per service but no object-level list for the OPS objects.
proposed: Let the per-service DB stories assign each of the 24 operational objects to its service schema; the wave-1 integration run asserts the 92 tables and every object that names a data product, records the 24 as an open list and does not fail on them.

title: deliverFile manifest payload, claim-check handoff and the file-window trigger contract are not defined
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 16 and 44; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 007 Integration adapters for file loads and outbound files v1.md sections 12 and 13
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 12.5 Workflows and activities; 12.6 Schedules; 13 Solution plan
description: Architecture v5 names the P2 activity deliverFile(manifest) and the activity receiveFile on queue rwb-integration, and says that Airflow opens the WIN file window at 16:00 and the buyer files per lot, but no source defines the payload of the manifest for this path, the claim-check handoff between rwb-integration and rwb-document (who creates the document ID, who issues the SAS link, how long it lives and how the bytes reach Blob), or the exact trigger contract of the two windows (what Airflow calls, with which parameters, and what happens when a window is missed). The legacy story defines OutboundFiles.enqueue and OutboundFileAdapter.send instead, and the reporting extract and the decision and outcome feed have no file definition left once the data lake is removed (DP-17).
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11 names only the file contract fields fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count plus a SAS link for one file valid 15 minutes; slide 16 lists Act: deliverFile(manifest), receiveFile and Airflow window: WIN file 16:00, buyer files per lot; slide 44 lists JOB-10 WIN notices 16:00 under rwb-comms and integration with mechanism Airflow file window plus workers. Legacy RWB-E1-007 section 12 defines OutboundFiles.enqueue, OutboundFileAdapter.send and four Quartz jobs (JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-13, JOB-15) and section 13 builds the two admin endpoints only.
proposed: Fix the deliverFile manifest schema, the claim-check handoff and the two window calls at the P2 contract review (RWB-P2-E1007-CON) and publish them in the activity contract jar and the AsyncAPI document before the first SIT run of this path.

title: The target read operation that serves the case list and the path by which the daily extract reaches rwb-reporting once the data lake is removed are not defined in the source documents
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 002 Case list v1 with case ID owner and queue v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 13-20, 41-44); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md
section: 2 Business rationale; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.3 Events published; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story builds the case list from the P3 in-process interface CaseQueryApi.openCaseAccounts(businessDate) and publishes the extract file to the data lake through the outbound file adapter (INT-19). Architecture v5 removes the in-process interface in favour of the rwb-case REST contract under /api/recovery/case/v1 and removes the data lake, INT-19 and INT-20 (DP-17, ADR-018), so reporting is fed from events into rwb-reporting; the deck names the rwb-integration deliverFile activity and the FileDelivered and FileFailed events but no source states which rwb-case read operation serves the case list that rwb-source-data builds for JOB-04, nor the target, the manifest fields or the receiving operation by which the business-date extract reaches rwb-reporting once the lake is gone. The case list reads of this integration story and the delivery assertion cannot be written against a contract no source fixes.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-002 section 12 Published interface used (CaseQueryApi.openCaseAccounts(businessDate)) and Flow step 9 (the extract file for the business date goes to the data lake through the outbound file adapter); Architecture v5 slides 13 and 14 (rwb-case IN: REST GET /cases/{id}, /cases?queue=), slide 15 (rwb-integration Table: Act deliverFile(manifest), EVT FileDelivered, FileFailed; rwb-reporting: Integration deliverFile (regulatory extract)), slide 18 (Suite Preface) slide 37 (data lake and Power BI not connected, INT-19/INT-20 removed) and slide 44 (JOB-04 event-triggered workflow in rwb-source-data); no AsyncAPI or OpenAPI document in the source set names the JOB-04 read operation or the rwb-reporting receipt.
proposed: Agree at the wave-1 contract review that JOB-04 reads the open case accounts through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases and the queue cut through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases on the rwb-case base /api/recovery/case/v1, and that the daily extract reaches rwb-reporting through the rwb-integration deliverFile activity on queue rwb-integration with a manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count, rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1 and rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1 on rwb.integration.events.v1 and a projection in schema rwb_reporting, with no data lake path. Publish the two contracts so this suite asserts them.

title: Owner of REC-03 and REC-04 and the reporting delivery path of the two extracts are not named for the microservice target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 011 Reconciliation and data quality report v1.md (sections 3, 4, 12 and 13)
description: The legacy story runs REC-01 to REC-05 inside one module and writes the reconciliation and data quality extracts to the data lake through the outbound adapter INT-19. The target removes the lake (DP-17, ADR-018) and splits the checks across services, but no source names which service runs REC-03 (treatments, S2 rwb-treatment) and REC-04 (payments, P8 rwb-payment), nor how the two extracts reach rwb-reporting once the lake is gone. The story therefore runs REC-03 and REC-04 as NOT_RUN with their reason in wave 1 and proves the target delivery through the rwb-integration deliverFile activity and the rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1 event.
evidence: Legacy section 4 steps 5 to 7 and 11 (one run writes every check and puts both extracts in the lake), section 12 (Output: the two extracts to the data lake through INT-19), section 13 (ReconciliationExtractWriter); Arch v5 slide 15 (P1 owns reconciliation, P9 reporting), slide 16 (P2 deliverFile, FileDelivered and FileFailed), slide 37 and slide 44 JOB-15 (no data lake); DP-17.
proposed: Confirm the owning service and the contract for REC-03 and REC-04 when rwb-treatment and rwb-payment enter wave 2, and fix the extract delivery as a deliverFile manifest from rwb-source-data to rwb-reporting through rwb-integration; keep NOT_RUN and its reason as the legacy BR10 value until then.

title: The connection matrix does not show the rwb-source-data outbound reads and the exclusion operation of the case contract is not named
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 13, 15 and 41); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 011 Reconciliation and data quality report v1.md (section 12)
description: REC-01 needs the accounts excluded at entry from case_entry_exclusion (P3) and REC-05 needs the asset keys (S5) and the notice person keys (P6), and the target rule is one hop on the owner contract with a 2 s timeout. Slide 13 of Arch v5 shows the rwb-source-data row with SQL access to the ACE database only and no REST or Temporal call to another service, and no source names the exclusion operation of the case contract, so neither the calling service nor the path of the exclusion read is fixed. The story takes rwb-source-data as the caller, one hop with a 2 s timeout, and cites the exclusion path as the one the P3 E1011 contract must publish.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 13 (P1 row: S to the ACE database only), slide 15 (P1 IN: /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}, /collateral/{id}, /payments, /freshness; OUT: reconciliation in rwb_source_data), slide 41 (P1 owns ACE view contract, extension tables, freshness, reconciliation); legacy section 12 (published interface of P3, excludedAccountsByProduct) and section 13 (ReferentialCheck); DP-01, DP-05, DP-11; Ownership Map case_entry_exclusion owner P3.
proposed: Add the three outbound reads of JOB-04 to the rwb-source-data row of the connection matrix and publish the exclusion resource on the rwb-case contract with its path, its fields and its 2 s budget.

title: Connection matrix gives rwb-integration only the document REST call and the outside file edge, while the file build reads source data and the failure reaches rwb-case
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 13 (connection matrix) against slides 11, 12, 15 and 16; Template and Rules v1 DP-05 and DP-11
section: 4 Flow; 8 BR11; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.4 Events consumed
description: The connection matrix on slide 13 gives the P2 Integration row only R (REST) to P5 and F (file) to outside, with no cell for P1 or P3. Slide 12 says any service that needs ACE data asks rwb-source-data, slide 15 gives rwb-source-data the freshness, customer and account reads, and slide 16 gives rwb-integration the activity deliverFile and the events FileDelivered and FileFailed. The legacy story read recovery.v_ace_contact, v_ace_account and v_ace_batch_status in process. This story follows slides 12 and 15 and DP-11, so the file build reads freshness, customer and account facts through the rwb-source-data base one hop with a 2 s timeout; the matrix cells for P2 to P1 and for the FileFailed listen edge of rwb-case are recorded as incomplete rather than prohibitive.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 13 table: the P2 Integration row shows R in the P5 column and F in the Outside column and no entry elsewhere, while the P3 Case row shows no entry in the P2 column; slide 12 (Need ACE data? Ask rwb-source-data: REST for screens, activity in workflows; only rwb-source-data reads the SQL views); slide 15 P1 IN REST GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}, /freshness; slide 16 P2 EVT FileDelivered, FileFailed. Legacy RWB-E1-007 section 4 steps 3 and 4 read the views in process.
proposed: Update the P2 row of the connection matrix at the architecture review to show its read path to rwb-source-data and the FileFailed edge into rwb-case, or make the requesting service pass the figures in the manifest; until then the rwb-source-data contract stays the only read path of the build.
